svg.text: Interface connector (one per signal group; arrow = active to passive)

Four channel, filter, and capture FIFO instances are represented by instance banks; each channel has its own mode, filter state, timestamp FIFO, and status. The shared counter update event reaches the IRQ aggregator through the channel/status bank. DMA data moves through memory-mapped timer data ports; the two req/ack pairs carry DMA request control, not payload data. APB/core CDC and DMA data-port placement remain open design details.
Structural timer top. APB controls software-visible registers and DMA data ports; timer-core logic handles counting, channel events, DMA queues,
Accepts APB accesses, stores software configuration and status, and bridges data-port operations across the selected clock profile.
Generates the shared prescaled 32-bit timebase, direction-dependent terminal count, reload, and update event.
Four independent instances synchronize each asynchronous input, sample it at the selected divider, and accept a level after the configured
Four independent channel instances select capture, output-compare, or edge-aligned PWM and report channel-local and shared update status.
Four independent depth-four queues retain capture timestamps and preserve older entries on overflow while setting a sticky overrun cause.
Arbitrates tagged queues and exposes two DMA request groups with configurable one-to-four-record bursts, metadata-first framing, and
Combines enabled channel, overrun, compare, and update causes into one level-sensitive interrupt output.
SoC -> timer: i_paddr_apb, i_psel_apb, i_penable_apb, i_pwrite_apb, i_pwdata_apb, i_pstrb_apb, i_pprot_apb; timer -> SoC: o_pready_apb,
timer req -> DMA; DMA ack -> timer
timer -> DMA: o_dma_cap_req; DMA -> timer: i_dma_cap_ack
timer req -> DMA; DMA ack -> timer
timer -> DMA: o_dma_cmp_req; DMA -> timer: i_dma_cmp_ack
DMA requester through APB -> timer data queues
